steps.message:
Redoak's addendum on Bent 2 came in April 21, 2026 and I want the foundation side closed out before the claim package goes to Council. Tell me whether the Bent 2 shafts are adequate as designed, and what the contract requires of us if they aren't. Redoak_Addendum_2026-04-21.pdf and Sub_DrilledShafts.pdf are on the share with the rest of the project record.

One memo to DeLuca for my signature, dated May 15, 2026. 
Save it as Bent2_Shaft_Determination.docx.

    This installation plan describes the equipment, materials, sequence, quality control, and inspection procedures
    Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC will follow to construct the twelve (12) drilled shafts required for the new Pecan
    Creek Bridge on Project WP-2401. The plan is submitted for the Engineer's review in accordance with
    Specification Section 421.2 (Contractor Submittals) and the drilled-shaft submittal requirements of Sheet B-17,
    prior to shaft production.

    1.2 Structures Covered
    The bridge foundation consists of twelve production drilled shafts distributed across the substructure as follows:

              Substructure Unit                  Station   Shafts    Governing Boring          Plan Reference

              Abutment 1 (west)                  167+00      4               B-1                  Sheet B-03

              Bent 1                             167+90      2               B-6                  Sheet B-05

              Bent 2                             168+95      2               B-7                  Sheet B-04

              Abutment 2 (east)                  169+85      4               B-8                  Sheet B-06

              Total                                         12                                    Sheet B-16

    All shafts are 48-inch nominal diameter with an 8-ft minimum rock socket into sound limestone as required by
    Spec 421.5(C) and Sheet B-17, Note 1.

    1.3 Design Assumptions Adopted from the Plans
    The installation plan is built to the design assumptions carried on Sheets B-04, B-16, and B-17 and Section 7.3
    of the Redoak Geotechnical Report:
         • Shaft diameter: 48-inch, all twelve shafts.
         • Rock socket: 8-ft minimum, measured from the actual encountered top of sound Class II or better
         limestone.
         • Allowable end bearing: 40 ksf in sound limestone. Side friction below the top of rock is neglected in the
         design; end bearing governs.
         • Concrete: Class C, f'c = 4,500 psi at 28 days, placement by tremie or with free-fall not exceeding 5 ft
         (Sheet B-17, Note 4).
         • Reinforcing: 20 - #11 longitudinal bars full length; #5 spiral at 4"/6"/4" per Sheet B-04.
         • Vertical datum: NAVD 88. All elevations in this submittal are on NAVD 88 in accordance with Sheet
         G-02 of the plans.
    The specific design elevations at Bent 2 (which control the shafts within the channel and are the most critical
    from a schedule standpoint) are carried through this plan as follows:
         • Design top of rock, Bent 2: 512.3 ft (NAVD 88), per Boring B-7.
         • Design shaft tip, Bent 2: 504.3 ft (NAVD 88), 8.0 ft below top of rock.
         • Allowable end bearing at Bent 2: 40 ksf.
    These values are consistent with the schedule on Sheet B-16 and the notes on Sheet B-04. Corresponding design
    elevations for Bent 1, Abutment 1, and Abutment 2 are tabulated in Section 4.1 of this plan.

         • Maximum torque: 250,000 ft-lb (continuous), 300,000 ft-lb (peak).

         27 ft below existing ground at Bent 2 to design tip).

    The Watson CLM-25 has performed comparable 48-inch rock-socketed shafts on Vantera's previous
    limestone-formation bridge projects; representative production records are attached in Appendix A.

    2.2 Tooling — Overburden
    For overburden and weathered material above sound rock:
         • 48-inch double-cut soil auger (single-flight, hardened cutting teeth) for excavation of overburden clays
         and weathered limestone.
         • 48-inch clean-out (muck) bucket for bailing loose cuttings and standing water from the hole bottom
         before advancing.
         • 48-inch belling bucket: not required by design; not deployed on this project.

    For excavation of sound limestone (rock socket):

         • 48-inch core barrel: single-wall calyx-style core barrel, 48-inch outside diameter, with tungsten-carbide
         cutting shoe. Used when full-face rock auger progress falls below Vantera's minimum production rate (0.5
         ft per 15 minutes of rotation) or when Engineer directs coring of a specific interval to verify rock quality.

    site throughout rock-socket operations. Tool inspection log is included in Appendix D.

    the ordinary high water elevation and 2.9 ft below the 100-year water surface elevation of 522.4 ft. The

    demobilization procedure is described in Vantera's SWPPP and Section 10 of this plan.

    4.3 Standard Installation Sequence for Each Shaft
    Each of the 12 shafts will be constructed following the sequence below. Deviations for a given shaft (e.g.,
    presence of standing water requiring slurry, or refusal on rock at other than design elevation) are handled by the
    decision procedures in Sections 5 and 6.
      Step 1 — Layout and Set Casing. Survey shaft center; check plumbness of leads. Drive or press temporary
      casing (see Section 5).
      Step 2 — Overburden Excavation. Drill overburden with the 48-inch double-cut soil auger under the
      protection of the temporary casing. Muck cuttings clear of the hole. Casing is advanced or held stationary as
      required to keep the top of overburden from sloughing.
      Step 3 — Top-of-Rock Confirmation. As drilling approaches the design top-of-rock elevation, the rig
      operator will slow the rate of advance and monitor drilling resistance, torque draw, and cuttings character.
      When sound limestone is encountered, drilling stops. The Field Inspector is called, and cuttings are compared
      with the boring log at that location. Actual top-of-rock elevation is recorded on the shaft log.
      Step 4 — Rock-Socket Excavation. Switch to the 48-inch full-face rock auger. Advance the socket 8 ft below
      the actual encountered top of rock; if partial-face conditions or a hard seam are encountered, switch to the
      48-inch core barrel to complete the socket. Log cuttings and drilling behavior in half-foot increments.

2.3 Response to Item 3 — Variability Disclosed in the Report
The Contract Documents also disclose that the top-of-rock surface across this corridor is variable. Section §5.2 of the sealed Redoak Geotechnical
Investigation Report (“Pinnacled-Limestone Variability”) states, in operative part:
         “…top-of-rock may fluctuate ±6 ft over ~30-ft lateral offsets due to karst weathering; localized rises and pinnacles common. Contractor
         should anticipate variable drilling behavior.”
Section §5.2 further advises the Contractor, in the subsections immediately following the quoted sentence, that (a) the actual top of rock at each
production shaft may differ from the log at the nearest boring by an amount within the range noted above; (b) pinnacled top of rock and karst features —
including clay-seam runs and localized voids — are inherent to the Edwards Group at this site, and variable drilling behavior (rapid transitions from soft
residuum into hard limestone, sudden loss of auger torque across seams, and short “false-refusal” pinnacles above the sound-rock horizon) should be
anticipated; and (c) field verification of sound-rock elevation at each production shaft is required, and equipment capable of handling both
hard-limestone drilling and soft-seam clean-out within the same shaft without extended re-mobilization should be provided.
Bent 2 lies within the corridor of §5.2 applicability. The nearest borings to Bent 2 are B-6 (Bent 1, Sta. 167+90; top of rock 510.7 ft NAVD 88)
approximately 105 ft west, and B-8 (Abut. 2, Sta. 169+85; top of rock 511.9 ft NAVD 88) approximately 90 ft east. The top-of-rock elevations logged at
B-6, B-7, and B-8 are internally consistent with the ±6 ft over ~30-ft-offset variability disclosed in §5.2.

     1. INTRODUCTION
    1.1 Project Description
    Redoak Geoscience LLC (Redoak) was retained by Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. (Larkspur) to perform a
    geotechnical investigation and prepare foundation and earthwork recommendations for the City of Milbrook's
    Wren Parkway Widening and Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement, Project No. WP-2401. The project extends
    approximately 2.4 miles (12,600 ft) along Wren Parkway between the Old Millican Road intersection (Sta.
    100+00, west limit) and the McKinney Boulevard intersection (Sta. 226+00, east limit), all within the City of
    Milbrook, Hays County, Texas.
    The existing 2-lane rural section is to be widened to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft shoulders and 6-ft
    sidewalks. The existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge over Pecan Creek (approximately 120 ft in length) is
    to be removed and replaced with a new 3-span prestressed concrete girder bridge, 285 ft in total length, on
    drilled-shaft foundations. Two abutments (Abut. 1 at Sta. 167+00 west and Abut. 2 at Sta. 169+85 east) and two
    intermediate bents (Bent 1 at Sta. 167+90 and Bent 2 at Sta. 168+95) frame the crossing.
    Additional geotechnical scope elements evaluated in this report include: two segmental retaining walls along
    the corridor (Reach R-1 near Sta. 128+00 and Reach R-2 near Sta. 152+00–154+00), embankment for the
    west-approach bridge fill (Sta. 165+50 to Abut. 1), pavement subgrade evaluation along the widening, and
    rock-controlled scour input at the Pecan Creek crossing.

    1.2 Scope of Services
    Redoak's scope, per the executed subconsultant agreement dated 04/09/2024, comprised the following:
        • Twelve (12) borings totaling approximately 495 linear feet, split between corridor and bridge stations.
        Rock coring using an NQ-3 (2.0-inch) triple-tube barrel was performed at all bridge and retaining-wall
        borings once auger refusal was encountered.
        • Standard Penetration Tests (SPT) in cohesive and granular overburden at 2.5- to 5-ft intervals per ASTM
        D1586.
        • Continuous split-spoon and Shelby-tube sampling as directed for laboratory testing, per ASTM D1587.
        • Rock coring per ASTM D2113 with Rock Quality Designation (RQD) logged in the field.
        • Laboratory testing for classification, strength, corrosivity, and rock unconfined compressive strength
        (UCS), per ASTM methods listed in Section 3.
        • Engineering analysis and preparation of this sealed report, including foundation recommendations,
        subgrade and retaining-wall input, scour parameters, and construction considerations.
        • One (1) design coordination meeting with Larkspur design staff during report development (held
        07/29/2024).
    Post-design (construction-phase) services — including shaft installation observation, load-test review if elected
    by Owner, and addenda in response to Contractor RFIs — are outside the base scope and available under
    separate authorization.

    1.3 Authorization
    Work was authorized under Larkspur Purchase Order LP-24-0417 dated 04/12/2024, executed against the
    Master Subconsultant Services Agreement between Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. and Redoak Geoscience LLC
    dated 03/01/2023. The City of Milbrook is the ultimate Owner; Larkspur is the prime consultant and addressee
    of this report.

    geotechnical investigation and prepare foundation and earthwork recommendations for the City of Milbrook's
    Wren Parkway Widening and Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement, Project No. WP-2401. The project extends
    approximately 2.4 miles (12,600 ft) along Wren Parkway between the Old Millican Road intersection (Sta.
    100+00, west limit) and the McKinney Boulevard intersection (Sta. 226+00, east limit), all within the City of
    Milbrook, Hays County, Texas.
    The existing 2-lane rural section is to be widened to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft shoulders and 6-ft
    sidewalks. The existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge over Pecan Creek (approximately 120 ft in length) is
    to be removed and replaced with a new 3-span prestressed concrete girder bridge, 285 ft in total length, on
    drilled-shaft foundations. Two abutments (Abut. 1 at Sta. 167+00 west and Abut. 2 at Sta. 169+85 east) and two
    intermediate bents (Bent 1 at Sta. 167+90 and Bent 2 at Sta. 168+95) frame the crossing.
    Additional geotechnical scope elements evaluated in this report include: two segmental retaining walls along
    the corridor (Reach R-1 near Sta. 128+00 and Reach R-2 near Sta. 152+00–154+00), embankment for the
    west-approach bridge fill (Sta. 165+50 to Abut. 1), pavement subgrade evaluation along the widening, and
    rock-controlled scour input at the Pecan Creek crossing.

    1.2 Scope of Services
    Redoak's scope, per the executed subconsultant agreement dated 04/09/2024, comprised the following:
        • Twelve (12) borings totaling approximately 495 linear feet, split between corridor and bridge stations.
        Rock coring using an NQ-3 (2.0-inch) triple-tube barrel was performed at all bridge and retaining-wall
        borings once auger refusal was encountered.
        • Standard Penetration Tests (SPT) in cohesive and granular overburden at 2.5- to 5-ft intervals per ASTM
        D1586.
        • Continuous split-spoon and Shelby-tube sampling as directed for laboratory testing, per ASTM D1587.
        • Rock coring per ASTM D2113 with Rock Quality Designation (RQD) logged in the field.
        • Laboratory testing for classification, strength, corrosivity, and rock unconfined compressive strength
        (UCS), per ASTM methods listed in Section 3.
        • Engineering analysis and preparation of this sealed report, including foundation recommendations,
        subgrade and retaining-wall input, scour parameters, and construction considerations.
        • One (1) design coordination meeting with Larkspur design staff during report development (held
        07/29/2024).
    Post-design (construction-phase) services — including shaft installation observation, load-test review if elected
    by Owner, and addenda in response to Contractor RFIs — are outside the base scope and available under
    separate authorization.

    1.3 Authorization
    Work was authorized under Larkspur Purchase Order LP-24-0417 dated 04/12/2024, executed against the
    Master Subconsultant Services Agreement between Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. and Redoak Geoscience LLC
    dated 03/01/2023. The City of Milbrook is the ultimate Owner; Larkspur is the prime consultant and addressee
    of this report.




Redoak Geoscience LLC | RG-24-0187 | Wren Parkway (WP-2401)                                                         Page 7
     1.4 Vertical & Horizontal Datum
        • Vertical datum: NAVD 88. All elevations reported in this document, including top-of-rock elevations,
        groundwater levels, and shaft-tip recommendations, reference NAVD 88.
        • Horizontal datum: NAD 83, Texas State Plane Central Zone (US survey feet).
        • Boring locations were staked and elevations checked by Larkspur survey staff (surveyor of record: Beau
        Terlingua, RPLS #6612) on 05/09/2024. Redoak reviewed the resulting stakeout and used the surveyed
        elevations to compute the top-of-rock elevations reported in this document.
        • Users of this report and the boring logs are cautioned that certain legacy record documents (including the
        1998 utility as-built along Wren Parkway) were prepared in NGVD 29. Per Larkspur survey control, the
        conversion from NGVD 29 to NAVD 88 at this site is +0.83 ft. NGVD 29 elevations from legacy
        documents shall not be used interchangeably with elevations in this report.

    1.5 Limitations
    Subsurface conditions between and beyond the borings may differ from those disclosed by the borings; the
    interpretations herein reflect a professional judgment based on the data obtained. Karst-influenced limestone in
    particular is subject to lateral variability, as discussed in Section 5.2. This report was prepared for the exclusive
    use of Larkspur Civil Group and the City of Milbrook on Project WP-2401. Recommendations should be
    re-evaluated if project geometry, loading, or design assumptions change materially, or if conditions encountered
    during construction differ from those described. Redoak should be retained to observe foundation installation
    and to confirm bearing conditions in the field.




Redoak Geoscience LLC | RG-24-0187 | Wren Parkway (WP-2401)                                                            Page 8
     2. FIELD INVESTIGATION
    2.1 Boring Program Overview
    Twelve (12) borings, designated B-1 through B-12, were completed between 05/13/2024 and 06/14/2024.
    Boring locations were chosen jointly by Larkspur and Redoak to (i) bracket the widening corridor, (ii) place a
    boring at each major bridge substructure location (both abutments and both interior bents), (iii) support
    retaining-wall design at Reaches R-1 and R-2, and (iv) characterize the west-approach embankment fill
    footprint.
    The bridge-adjacent borings — B-1 (Abut. 1), B-6 (Bent 1), B-7 (Bent 2), and B-8 (Abut. 2) — are the principal
    foundation borings. Each was extended a minimum of 20 ft into sound rock or to a total depth sufficient to core
    through pinnacle features and confirm continuity of the underlying limestone.

    2.2 Drilling Methods & Equipment
    Overburden was advanced using 4-1/4-inch inside-diameter hollow-stem augers on Redoak's CME-75
    truck-mounted rig (corridor stations) and CME-550 all-terrain rig (bridge and creek-side stations). Where
    cohesive soils permitted, wash-boring was used to advance the hole between sampling intervals. Rock coring
    commenced at auger refusal, using an NQ-3 (2.0-inch outside diameter) triple-tube wireline core barrel run in
    5-ft increments.
    Field crews were led by Redoak field geologists Kevin Rausch (PG #4118) and Amaya Simms (PG #6402),
    each of whom maintained continuous logs at the rig. All boring logs were reviewed and signed by the Engineer
    of Record following office review of the field logs, laboratory test results, and rock core photographs.

    2.3 Sampling & In-Situ Testing

                                                          SECTION 03300

                              CAST-IN-PLACE STRUCTURAL CONCRETE
 03300.01 — Description
 This Section governs the furnishing of materials, proportioning, mixing, placing, finishing, curing, and acceptance of
 cast-in-place structural concrete for retaining walls, bridge substructure elements (footings, columns, caps,
 wingwalls, and abutment stems), approach slabs, drainage structures, and miscellaneous structural concrete. Work
 shall conform to ACI 318, ACI 301, ACI 305R and ACI 306R as applicable, and AASHTO LRFD Bridge
 Construction Specifications, except where superseded by the requirements below.

 03300.02 — Mix Classes and Specified Strength
 Concrete shall be furnished in the mix classes tabulated below. The 28-day compressive strength (f′c) shown is the
 specified strength for acceptance under 03300.06.

             Class       Application                                                                    Specified 28-day f′c

                A        Bridge substructure — footings, columns, caps, abutment stems                         4,500 psi

                B        Retaining-wall stems and footings (Reaches R-1, R-2, R-3)                             4,000 psi

                C        Drainage structures, headwalls, junction boxes                                        3,500 psi

                D        Bridge deck (composite with prestressed girders)                                      4,500 psi

                E        Concrete pavement (see Section 401)                                               Per Section 401

                F        Sidewalks, driveways, non-structural flatwork                                         3,000 psi

 The retaining-wall mix (Class B) shall be proportioned to a specified 28-day compressive strength of 4,000 psi,
 with a maximum water-cementitious materials ratio of 0.45, minimum cement content of 611 lb/CY, entrained air
 5.5% ± 1.5%, and slump 4 in. ± 1 in. at the point of placement. Cementitious materials shall consist of Type I/II
 portland cement with a Class F fly ash replacement of not less than 20% and not more than 30% by mass of total
 cementitious materials.

 03300.03 — Submittals
 Mix designs shall be submitted to the Engineer for each class not less than 30 calendar days prior to first placement.
 Each mix design shall include:
         (a) Trial batch data with 28-day cylinder breaks demonstrating a strength margin (f′cr) computed per ACI 301
         §4.2.3;
         (b) Certified aggregate gradations, specific gravities, and absorption;
         (c) Admixture certifications (Type A, D, F, or G per ASTM C494);
         (d) Statement of proposed batch plant, transit time to site, and placement rate;
         (e) Curing plan.
 No placement shall proceed against an unapproved mix design.

 03300.04 — Batching, Delivery, and Placement


Technical Specifications — Book 2 of 2 • FINAL — Issued for Bid • October 15, 2024                                                    Page 3
 Larkspur Civil Group, Inc.                                                  Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement — WP-2401



 Batching shall conform to ASTM C94. Time from introduction of mixing water to completion of discharge shall not
 exceed 90 minutes (60 minutes when ambient temperature exceeds 85 °F). Water added at the site to restore slump
 shall not cause the water-cementitious ratio to exceed the mix design value; retempering with water is prohibited.
 Placement in lifts shall not exceed 12 ft in vertical rise. Consolidation shall be by internal vibration; the Contractor
 shall have redundant vibrators on-site during placement. Cold-weather placement (ambient < 40 °F or falling to < 40
 °F within 24 hours) shall follow ACI 306R; hot-weather placement (ambient > 90 °F or forecast to exceed 90 °F
 within 24 hours) shall follow ACI 305R.

 03300.05 — Curing
 All structural concrete shall be moist-cured or membrane-cured for a minimum of 7 calendar days. Water curing is
 required for bridge decks and for any Class A element with an exposed face wider than 3 ft. Curing compounds shall
 be Type 2 (white pigmented) conforming to ASTM C309.

 03300.06 — Acceptance and Strength Evaluation
 03300.06.A — Sampling
 Concrete shall be sampled per ASTM C172 at the point of discharge into the forms. Frequency of sampling for
 acceptance shall be:
         (a) One set (four cylinders) per 50 CY placed, but not less than one set per placement per class per day;
         (b) Two cylinders shall be tested at 28 days for acceptance; one at 7 days for information; one held as a
         laboratory reserve.
 Cylinders shall be cast, cured, transported, and tested per ASTM C31 and ASTM C39 by the Owner's independent
 materials testing laboratory (Pinnacle Testing Services LLC). The average of the two 28-day cylinders from one
 sample constitutes a strength test for purposes of this Section.

 03300.06.B — Acceptance Criteria for Strength
 The strength of each class of concrete shall be considered satisfactory when both of the following are met:
         (a) No individual 28-day strength test result falls more than 500 psi below the specified compressive strength
         f′c. For the Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this means no individual strength test result
         shall fall below 3,500 psi.
         (b) The average of any three consecutive strength tests equals or exceeds the specified compressive strength
         f′c.
 Failure to satisfy criterion (a) — that is, the occurrence of any individual test result more than 500 psi below the
 specified strength — shall be cause for the Engineer to require an investigation of the strength of the concrete in
 place, in accordance with ACI 318 §26.12 and 03300.06.C below. Failure to satisfy criterion (b) shall require the
 Contractor to take steps to raise the average strength of subsequent production.

 03300.06.C — Investigation of Low-Strength Test Results — Core Sampling
 When an individual strength test falls more than 500 psi below the specified strength, or when there is other cause to
 doubt the strength of concrete in place, the Engineer may direct that the strength of the concrete in place be evaluated
 by drilled cores taken and tested per ASTM C42. Cores shall be drilled from the questioned placement not sooner
 than 14 calendar days after placement (measured from placement date to core-drilling date) and not later than 45
 calendar days after placement, unless otherwise directed by the Engineer.
 Three cores shall be taken from the area represented by the failing strength test. The location and orientation of cores
 shall be selected by the Engineer to represent the questioned concrete without compromising the structural integrity

 of the element. Core holes shall be filled with a non-shrink structural grout of strength not less than the specified
 strength f′c.
 The concrete in the area represented by a set of three cores shall be considered structurally adequate — and the
 placement shall be accepted in place — when both of the following are satisfied:
         (a) The average compressive strength of the three cores equals or exceeds 85% of the specified strength
         (0.85 × f′c). For the Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this threshold is 3,400 psi.
         (b) No individual core has a compressive strength less than 75% of the specified strength (0.75 × f′c). For the
         Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this threshold is 3,000 psi.
 Core results shall be corrected for length-to-diameter ratio per ASTM C42 §7.7 before comparison to these criteria.
 Cores that do not satisfy both criteria shall be cause for the Engineer to require load testing, structural analysis
 reduction, replacement of the concrete, or such other remedial measures as the Engineer determines are required to
 establish the structural adequacy of the element.

 03300.06.D — Payment During Investigation
 No payment shall be made for concrete under investigation until the investigation is concluded and the Engineer has
 issued a written disposition. When cores establish that the placement is acceptable in place under 03300.06.C, no
 reduction in payment shall be taken solely on account of low cylinder breaks; the placement shall be paid as bid.
 Nothing in 03300.06 relieves the Contractor of the obligation to furnish concrete meeting the specified strength at the
 point of delivery. Repeated occurrences of individual test failures against criterion (a) shall be cause for the Engineer
 to direct that the mix design be re-proportioned and re-submitted before further placement.

 03300.07 — Tolerances
 Formed surface tolerances shall meet ACI 117 Class B for concealed backfilled surfaces and Class A for
 architecturally exposed surfaces. Vertical alignment tolerance for retaining-wall stems shall not exceed 1 in. in 10 ft,
 and not more than 2 in. cumulative over any single stem lift.

 03300.08 — Method of Measurement and Payment
 Cast-in-place structural concrete shall be measured by the cubic yard, computed from plan dimensions, of each class
 in place and accepted. Payment shall be at the contract unit price per cubic yard for the class furnished and includes
 all forming, reinforcement placement supervision, batching, mixing, transporting, placing, consolidating, finishing,
 curing, cylinder casting cooperation, and appurtenant work. Reinforcement is paid separately under Section 03200.

                                                            SECTION 401

                             PORTLAND CEMENT CONCRETE PAVEMENT
 401.01 — Description
 This Section governs construction of jointed plain concrete pavement (JPCP) for the widened travel lanes of Wren
 Parkway between Stations 100+00 and 226+00, including the bridge-approach transition slabs. Work shall conform
 to AASHTO M 148, AASHTO M 249, ACI 325.12R, and the standard details in Sheets D-1 through D-6 of the
 Contract Drawings.

 401.02 — Materials
 Cement: Type I/II portland cement conforming to ASTM C150. Blended cements per ASTM C595 (Type IL) may
 be substituted with the Engineer's written approval.
 Coarse Aggregate: Crushed limestone conforming to ASTM C33 Size No. 57 or No. 67. Los Angeles abrasion loss
 (ASTM C131) shall not exceed 40%. Micro-Deval loss (ASTM D6928) shall not exceed 18%.
 Fine Aggregate: Natural sand conforming to ASTM C33 with fineness modulus between 2.6 and 3.0.
 Admixtures: Air-entraining admixture per ASTM C260. Water-reducing admixtures per ASTM C494 Types A, D,
 or F.
 Reinforcement: Deformed epoxy-coated dowel bars per ASTM A615 Grade 60 with ASTM A934 coating, 1-1/2

    1. INTRODUCTION
    1.1 Project Description
    The City of Milbrook is replacing the existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge (approximately 120 ft in
    length) carrying Wren Parkway over Pecan Creek with a new 3-span prestressed concrete girder bridge, 285 ft
    in total length. The new structure is founded on 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 8 ft into sound
    limestone at an allowable end bearing of 40 ksf. The two abutments (Abut. 1 at Sta. 167+00 west and Abut. 2 at
    Sta. 169+85 east) and two intermediate bents (Bent 1 at Sta. 167+90 and Bent 2 at Sta. 168+95) frame the
    crossing. Span lengths are 90 ft, 105 ft, and 90 ft, respectively.
    The project also widens Wren Parkway from a 2-lane rural section to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft
    shoulders and 6-ft sidewalks, over a total length of approximately 2.4 miles (Sta. 100+00 to Sta. 226+00).
    Roadway widening does not materially alter the drainage area contributing to Pecan Creek at the crossing.

    1.2 Purpose and Scope
    The purpose of this evaluation is to:
      • Establish design hydraulic conditions at Pecan Creek for the 100-year storm event, per FHWA HEC-18
         Chapter 5;
      • Compute contraction, local (pier), and abutment scour components in accordance with FHWA HEC-18;
      • Establish the design scour floor for the substructure and verify that foundation embedment at each bent and
         abutment is adequate;
      • Specify riprap gradation, thickness, filter, and extent at abutments per FHWA HEC-23 Design Guideline
         11;
      • Document the technical basis for the conformed countermeasure detail shown on Sheet S-3R (Rev 1) of the
         IFC plan set.

    2. METHODOLOGY
    2.1 HEC-18 Framework
    FHWA HEC-18 organizes bridge scour analysis into three superposed components — contraction scour, local
    scour at piers, and local scour at abutments — evaluated at the design flood and, where applicable, checked at
    the check flood. Long-term aggradation and degradation and lateral migration of the channel are evaluated
    separately from event-driven scour (§2.2 of HEC-18) and are treated in Section 9 of this report.
    The design flood for scour on a new bridge over Pecan Creek is the 100-year event, consistent with FHWA
    guidance (HEC-18 Chapter 2) for a bridge of this classification and its role in the City's arterial network. A
    check flood (500-year event) was evaluated separately and does not govern foundation embedment at this site;
    results are summarized qualitatively in this report but the 100-year event controls all design decisions
    documented herein.

    2.2 Total Scour Composition
    Design total scour depth (yt) at any given substructure element is the sum of:
      • y — Contraction scour (evaluated as either live-bed or clear-water per HEC-18 Ch. 6);
          c
      • y — Local (pier or abutment) scour (evaluated per HEC-18 Ch. 7 or 8, as applicable).
          s
    Long-term degradation, if any, is added separately. Aggradation is not credited against event scour for
    embedment purposes.
    The design scour floor at each substructure location is the ground/bed elevation reduced by the sum of these
    components, then compared against foundation tip elevation to verify embedment.

    2.3 HEC-23 Countermeasure Framework
    Riprap and companion countermeasures at abutments are sized per HEC-23 Volume 2, Design Guideline 11
    (Riprap at Bridge Abutments). The framework selects a median rock size (D50) based on the approach velocity
    and abutment geometry; specifies a graded gradation band; requires a filter (geotextile or graded aggregate);
    and specifies the horizontal extent and thickness of the blanket relative to the abutment footprint.
    Pier countermeasures are not employed at this crossing, because the local scour at the piers is rock-controlled at
    the top of sound limestone (see §2.4 and §6.3) and no supplemental scour countermeasure is required at the pier
    substructure.

    2.4 Rock-Controlled Scour Treatment (HEC-18 §6.8)
    HEC-18 §6.8 (Scour in Erodible Rock) recognizes that when erodible rock is encountered within the scour
    envelope, scour depth is limited by the rock's competence — its ability to resist detachment by the hydraulic
    loading — rather than by the empirical sand-and-gravel formulas of Chapters 6, 7, and 8. In sound, jointed
    limestone with high unconfined compressive strength (UCS), low weathering index (Slake Durability Id2), and
    adequate rock quality (RQD), the scour envelope terminates at the sound-rock surface for the design flood, and
    event-driven scour below that surface is negligible.
    The Redoak Geoscience LLC geotechnical investigation for Project WP-2401 (Report RG-24-0187, sealed
    08/22/2024) documents sound Edwards Group limestone underlying the Pecan Creek crossing, with
    geometric-mean UCS across the bridge-footprint borings B-1, B-6, B-7, and B-8 of approximately 11,180 psi (n
    = 8), RQD in sound rock averaging 78–84 percent, and Slake Durability Id2 ranging 94–97 percent (rated very
    high). Redoak concurs with modeling scour as rock-controlled at the sound-limestone surface for foundation
    embedment purposes (Redoak Report §8.1). This report incorporates that recommendation and applies HEC-18

    3. HYDROLOGY AND HYDRAULIC INPUTS
    3.1 Drainage Area and Storm Recurrence
    Pecan Creek at the Wren Parkway crossing drains an approximately 4.6-square-mile watershed originating in
    the low-relief limestone terrain west of Milbrook. Land cover is mixed suburban, pasture, and open-space, with
    modest impervious cover (approximately 21 percent per the 2022 City of Milbrook land-cover raster). The
    watershed is not gauged at the crossing; regional-regression hydrology and prior watershed studies performed
    by the City in 2019 (Pecan Creek Watershed Master Plan, HDR, 2019) are used as the primary hydrologic basis
    for design.
    The design storm for the bridge is the 100-year recurrence interval event, consistent with the City's design
    criteria for new arterial bridges over regulated streams.

    The 100-year peak discharge at the Pecan Creek / Wren Parkway crossing is:

    1. INTRODUCTION
    1.1 Project Description
    The City of Milbrook is replacing the existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge (approximately 120 ft in
    length) carrying Wren Parkway over Pecan Creek with a new 3-span prestressed concrete girder bridge, 285 ft
    in total length. The new structure is founded on 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 8 ft into sound
    limestone at an allowable end bearing of 40 ksf. The two abutments (Abut. 1 at Sta. 167+00 west and Abut. 2 at
    Sta. 169+85 east) and two intermediate bents (Bent 1 at Sta. 167+90 and Bent 2 at Sta. 168+95) frame the
    crossing. Span lengths are 90 ft, 105 ft, and 90 ft, respectively.
    The project also widens Wren Parkway from a 2-lane rural section to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft
    shoulders and 6-ft sidewalks, over a total length of approximately 2.4 miles (Sta. 100+00 to Sta. 226+00).
    Roadway widening does not materially alter the drainage area contributing to Pecan Creek at the crossing.

    1.2 Purpose and Scope
    The purpose of this evaluation is to:
      • Establish design hydraulic conditions at Pecan Creek for the 100-year storm event, per FHWA HEC-18
         Chapter 5;
      • Compute contraction, local (pier), and abutment scour components in accordance with FHWA HEC-18;
      • Establish the design scour floor for the substructure and verify that foundation embedment at each bent and
         abutment is adequate;
      • Specify riprap gradation, thickness, filter, and extent at abutments per FHWA HEC-23 Design Guideline
         11;
      • Document the technical basis for the conformed countermeasure detail shown on Sheet S-3R (Rev 1) of the
         IFC plan set.

         Design Guidance, 3rd Edition, Volumes 1 and 2 (Lagasse, Clopper, Pagán-Ortiz, Zevenbergen, Arneson,

    2. METHODOLOGY
    2.1 HEC-18 Framework
    FHWA HEC-18 organizes bridge scour analysis into three superposed components — contraction scour, local
    scour at piers, and local scour at abutments — evaluated at the design flood and, where applicable, checked at
    the check flood. Long-term aggradation and degradation and lateral migration of the channel are evaluated
    separately from event-driven scour (§2.2 of HEC-18) and are treated in Section 9 of this report.
    The design flood for scour on a new bridge over Pecan Creek is the 100-year event, consistent with FHWA
    guidance (HEC-18 Chapter 2) for a bridge of this classification and its role in the City's arterial network. A
    check flood (500-year event) was evaluated separately and does not govern foundation embedment at this site;
    results are summarized qualitatively in this report but the 100-year event controls all design decisions
    documented herein.

    2.2 Total Scour Composition
    Design total scour depth (yt) at any given substructure element is the sum of:
      • y — Contraction scour (evaluated as either live-bed or clear-water per HEC-18 Ch. 6);
          c
      • y — Local (pier or abutment) scour (evaluated per HEC-18 Ch. 7 or 8, as applicable).
          s
    Long-term degradation, if any, is added separately. Aggradation is not credited against event scour for
    embedment purposes.
    The design scour floor at each substructure location is the ground/bed elevation reduced by the sum of these
    components, then compared against foundation tip elevation to verify embedment.

    2.3 HEC-23 Countermeasure Framework
    Riprap and companion countermeasures at abutments are sized per HEC-23 Volume 2, Design Guideline 11
    (Riprap at Bridge Abutments). The framework selects a median rock size (D50) based on the approach velocity
    and abutment geometry; specifies a graded gradation band; requires a filter (geotextile or graded aggregate);
    and specifies the horizontal extent and thickness of the blanket relative to the abutment footprint.
    Pier countermeasures are not employed at this crossing, because the local scour at the piers is rock-controlled at
    the top of sound limestone (see §2.4 and §6.3) and no supplemental scour countermeasure is required at the pier
    substructure.

    2.4 Rock-Controlled Scour Treatment (HEC-18 §6.8)
    HEC-18 §6.8 (Scour in Erodible Rock) recognizes that when erodible rock is encountered within the scour
    envelope, scour depth is limited by the rock's competence — its ability to resist detachment by the hydraulic
    loading — rather than by the empirical sand-and-gravel formulas of Chapters 6, 7, and 8. In sound, jointed
    limestone with high unconfined compressive strength (UCS), low weathering index (Slake Durability Id2), and
    adequate rock quality (RQD), the scour envelope terminates at the sound-rock surface for the design flood, and
    event-driven scour below that surface is negligible.
    The Redoak Geoscience LLC geotechnical investigation for Project WP-2401 (Report RG-24-0187, sealed
    08/22/2024) documents sound Edwards Group limestone underlying the Pecan Creek crossing, with
    geometric-mean UCS across the bridge-footprint borings B-1, B-6, B-7, and B-8 of approximately 11,180 psi (n
    = 8), RQD in sound rock averaging 78–84 percent, and Slake Durability Id2 ranging 94–97 percent (rated very
    high). Redoak concurs with modeling scour as rock-controlled at the sound-limestone surface for foundation
    embedment purposes (Redoak Report §8.1). This report incorporates that recommendation and applies HEC-18

of November 20, 2026. This letter is submitted concurrently with, and is supported by, Vantera's written

The Engineer is respectfully requested to review, log, and forward this request to the City for action. Vantera
stands ready to meet at the Engineer's earliest convenience to walk through the supporting record.

1. Basis for the Time Extension Request
The requested 21 calendar days are wholly attributable to conditions encountered in the drilled-shaft foundation
work at Bent 2 of the Pecan Creek bridge replacement. Beginning the week of March 17, 2026, Vantera's drilling
subcontractor encountered materially harder rock, at a higher elevation and over a greater vertical interval, than
what a reasonable and prudent contractor would have anticipated from the contract documents and from the
sealed geotechnical report referenced in the Bid Documents. The impact on production has been documented in
the Engineer's daily reports, in Vantera's shift logs, and in Vantera's Notice under §4.3 dated April 10, 2026.
The critical path of the Project as reflected in Schedule Update 15 (data date April 30, 2026) runs directly through
the Bent 2 shaft cap → column → cap → girder erection → deck pour → approach slab sequence. Any impact to
Bent 2 shaft completion carries day-for-day into the critical path. Vantera's forensic time-impact analysis,
prepared consistent with recognized industry practice, calculates a net delay
to the critical path of 21 calendar days after accounting for concurrent activities and available non-critical
work-around. That analysis is offered without prejudice to any additional entitlement that may develop should the
condition persist beyond the anticipated completion of Bent 2 rock socket drilling.
The direct causes contributing to the 21-calendar-day impact are summarized as follows:
 •   Refusal at higher elevation than indicated. Rock refusal at Bent 2 was reached materially above the
     elevation indicated in the sealed geotechnical record on which Vantera reasonably relied during bidding.
     Detailed elevation data and Vantera's characterization of the encountered condition are set forth in the
     accompanying differing-site-conditions claim letter of even date.

         in Vantera's baseline schedule for a rock socket of the specified depth.
     •   Down-hole tooling change-out. The condition required a change from the initially mobilized rock-auger
         configuration to a core-barrel/roller-cone configuration, together with off-site sharpening cycles that were

  the Contract Sum in the amount of $487,600.00 and to a time extension of 21 calendar days.

  2. Contract Documents Relied Upon at Bid
  At the time of bid, Vantera relied upon the following portions of the Contract Documents in preparing its
  estimate for the Bent 2 drilled-shaft installation:

   •   The Foundation Plan, Sheet B-04 , showing the Bent 2 shaft geometry, tip elevation, and required rock
       socket in sound limestone;
   •   The Boring Location Plan bound with the Contract Documents;
   •   The geotechnical report prepared by the Engineer's subconsultant, which was included in the bid
       package and identified as the geotechnical basis of the foundation design;
   •   The technical specifications for drilled-shaft installation, rock excavation, and payment.

  The geotechnical report indicates, at the Bent 2 substructure location, a top-of-rock elevation of
  approximately 524 ft NAVD 88 with the top-of-sound-rock in the general elevation band shown on the
  Contract Documents. In relying on the geotechnical report at bid, Vantera developed unit crew
  productivities and tooling plans consistent with the depth-to-rock and rock-socket lengths represented by the
  Contract Documents.

  Vantera acknowledges the general limitations language customary to geotechnical reporting. That customary
  language does not, however, insulate the Owner from the operation of §4.3 where the actually-encountered
  condition is materially different from what the Contract Documents indicate.

  3. Condition Actually Encountered at Bent 2
  Drilled-shaft installation at Bent 2 was performed by Vantera's foundation crew using an IMT AF200 rotary
  drill with cross-cutter and rock auger tooling appropriate to the anticipated overburden and weathered-rock
  section. Shaft installation at Bent 2 commenced on 03/17/2026 following completion of Bent 1.

  The Bent 2 shaft advanced through overburden without incident to elevation approximately 518.4 ft NAVD
  88, at which point the crew encountered continuous, hard, unweathered limestone requiring a change from
  soil augering to rock-cutting tooling. The elevation at which continuous hard rock was first encountered at
  Bent 2 was surveyed by Vantera's field engineer on 03/17/2026 and independently confirmed on
  03/18/2026. Both measurements place the top of hard rock at 518.4 ft NAVD 88, referenced to the Contract
  vertical datum.

  The condition observed differs from that indicated in the Contract Documents in the following material
  respects:

   1. Elevation of top-of-rock. Top of hard rock at Bent 2 was encountered at 518.4 ft NAVD 88, which is
       approximately 6 feet higher in elevation than the top-of-rock elevation shown in the geotechnical
       report at the Bent 2 substructure location.

   2. Character of the rock at the encountered elevation. The rock first encountered was continuous,
       low-RQD-neutral, hard limestone requiring rock-cutter tooling from the initial contact — not the
       weathered-to-transitional profile the Contract Documents indicated would be present at the elevation at
       which rock was first encountered.
   3. Volume of rock excavation. The additional 6 vertical feet of rock, over the plan shaft diameter and
       across both shafts at Bent 2, materially increased the quantity of rock excavation required to reach the
       plan tip elevation compared to the quantity indicated by the Contract Documents.

  The 03/17/2026 daily inspection report prepared by the Engineer's field representative independently notes
  “hard drilling encountered above the anticipated top-of-rock elevation” at Bent 2, corroborating Vantera's
  observation.

  Vantera's field observations, the survey measurements taken on 03/17/2026 and 03/18/2026, and the
  rock-elevation survey data collectively establish that the encountered condition
  was materially different from those indicated in the Contract Documents. Accordingly, the encountered
  condition constitutes a differing site condition within the meaning of Contract §4.3.

  4. Impact on the Work
  The differing site condition impacted the Bent 2 shaft installation in the following respects:

  4.1 Additional rock drilling.
  The unanticipated 6 ft of hard-rock section above the elevation indicated by the Contract Documents
  required Vantera to drill an additional volume of rock at each of the Bent 2 shafts to reach the plan tip
  elevation. Rock drilling productivity in the encountered material was substantially lower than the
  productivity assumed at bid for the elevations in question, and the additional volume was not included in the
  bid quantities on which Vantera priced the drilled-shaft pay item.

  4.2 Tooling changes and wear.
  The encountered condition required Vantera to mobilize a supplemental rock-cutter head and a second set of
  teeth mid-shaft, and to demobilize and re-sharpen tooling twice within the Bent 2 sequence. Tooling wear
  costs incurred are substantially in excess of the tooling wear anticipated at bid for the Bent 2 shafts.

  4.3 Crew standby and re-sequencing.
  The change from soil-augering to rock-cutting mid-shaft, coupled with the additional tooling change
  described above, required the shaft crew to stand by while tooling was exchanged and re-sharpened, and
  required the concrete-placement subcontractor to be re-sequenced twice.

  4.4 Delay to the Bent 2 completion milestone.
  The additional rock drilling, tooling exchanges, and re-sequencing delayed the Bent 2 shaft completion
  milestone by 21 calendar days from the baseline schedule. Because Bent 2 is on the critical path for the
  substructure completion and for the subsequent superstructure erection, the delay to Bent 2 flows through
  directly to project Substantial Completion.

 CO-06 — Justification and Basis for Adjustment

 Weather data recorded at the National Weather Service Austin–Bergstrom station (KAUS), located approximately 22
 miles east-northeast of the project site, together with the on-site rain-gauge readings and daily reports (DR-0347
 through DR-0389), demonstrate the following excursions above the ten-year historical baseline for the December
 2025 – January 2026 period:
   •   December 22–24, 2025: Sustained minimum temperatures below 20°F for 62 consecutive hours, together with
       1.4 inches of freezing precipitation. Ten-year baseline for that calendar window is no more than 28 consecutive
       hours below 20°F and 0.4 inches freezing precipitation.
   •   January 8–14, 2026: Six calendar days with maximum temperature at or below 32°F, versus a baseline of two
       such days for the period.
   •   January 22–24, 2026: 2.9 inches of rainfall in 36 hours producing site-access closure to Bent 2 and R-2 work
       areas from an inundated construction road.
 Contract §8.3.1 and General Conditions §8.3.3 provide for compensable time extensions where the number of
 adverse weather days exceeds the historical baseline for the corresponding calendar period, without duplication with
 float. The Contractor's analysis identifies 28 calendar days attributable to weather impact on critical-path
 activities Bridge 3210 (Bent 2 Shaft Drilling), Bridge 3220 (Bent 2 Shaft Rebar and Concrete), and Roadway 2410
 (R-2 Concrete Placements W-08 through W-12).
 An additional 14 calendar days are attributable to reduced drilled-shaft production rates at Bent 2, measured as the
 difference between the baseline production of one shaft per 3.5 working days (as reflected in the Contractor's
 accepted baseline schedule) and the achieved rate during the 01/15/2026 – 01/28/2026 period of one shaft per 5.7
 working days on average. The Engineer has reviewed the drilling records, tool-log entries, and daily reports and
 concurs that the reduced production is attributable to formation hardness within the design profile and not to
 Contractor means-and-methods deficiencies. Nothing in this Change Order shall be construed as a determination of
 entitlement, or a waiver of the Owner's or Engineer's positions, with respect to any subsequent
 differing-site-conditions claim relating to the Bent 2 shafts.
 Total time extension: 42 calendar days, extending Substantial Completion from October 9, 2026 to November 20,
 2026. Total cost impact: $198,320.00, consisting of $121,540.00 in documented weather-related standby and
 remediation costs and $76,780.00 in production-loss compensation for drilled-shaft operations.
 Recommended by the Engineer for execution.

 5. ITEM 2 — BID ITEM 421 (DRILLED SHAFTS): CLARIFICATIONS
Bid item affected: Bid Item 421 — Drilled Shafts, 48-inch Diameter, Rock-Socketed (Bridge Foundations at Abut. 1, Bent 1, Bent 2, Abut. 2). Unit:
linear feet (LF) of completed shaft.
Purpose of clarification: Bidders raised questions at the Pre-Bid Meeting held on November 5, 2024, concerning (a) how the required 8-foot
minimum rock socket is measured and paid when the top of rock actually encountered differs from the design elevation, (b) whether temporary casing
is a separately paid item, (c) the treatment of rock coring where directed by the Engineer, and (d) sonic-integrity testing responsibility. The following
clarifications are issued to place all Bidders on equal footing. No change is made to the design diameter (48 inches), the minimum rock-socket length
(8 feet in sound limestone), or the allowable end bearing (40 ksf).
Clarification 2.1 — Design elevations for bidding. For the purpose of preparing the Bid, Bidders shall use the design top-of-rock and shaft-tip
elevations tabulated on Sheet B-16 (Foundation Plan — Drilled Shafts) and repeated below. All elevations are NAVD 88, consistent with the project
vertical datum stated on Sheet G-02.
                   Location              Boring          Top of Rock (NAVD 88)            Design Shaft Tip (NAVD 88)           Rock Socket
        Abut. 1 (west)                     B-1                    508.5 ft                          500.5 ft                       8.0 ft
        Bent 1                             B-6                    510.7 ft                          502.7 ft                       8.0 ft
        Bent 2                             B-7                   512.3 ft                           504.3 ft                       8.0 ft
        Abut. 2 (east)                     B-8                    511.9 ft                          503.9 ft                       8.0 ft

The 8-foot rock-socket length shown is a minimum. The design shaft-tip elevation is the design value at each location; the actual required tip is a
function of the top of rock actually encountered at each shaft.
Clarification 2.2 — Rock-socket length as measured in the field. The required 8-foot minimum rock socket shall be measured from the actual top of
sound Class II or better limestone encountered at each shaft — not from the design top-of-rock elevation shown on Sheet B-16 or on Sheet B-04 (Bent
2 Details). Where the top of rock is encountered above the design elevation, the shaft tip may be adjusted upward provided the 8-foot minimum
rock-socket length in sound limestone is preserved. Where the top of rock is encountered below the design elevation, the shaft tip shall be adjusted
downward such that the 8-foot minimum rock-socket length in sound limestone is preserved.
Consistent with Sheet B-17, Note 6, if the actual top of rock encountered differs from the design elevation shown on Sheet B-16 by more than 3 feet in
either direction, the Contractor shall stop and notify the Engineer prior to placement of concrete. The Engineer will determine, in writing, the required
shaft-tip elevation for the affected shaft.
Bidders are advised that the sealed Geotechnical Report by Redoak Geoscience LLC (Section 5.2) notes that pinnacled-limestone lateral variability
may reach ±6 feet over lateral offsets of approximately 30 feet, owing to karst weathering, and the design accommodates such variability by anchoring
the rock-socket requirement to the rock actually encountered.
Clarification 2.3 — Measurement and payment. Payment for Bid Item 421 shall be made at the Contract unit price per linear foot of completed drilled
shaft, measured from the design shaft-tip elevation to the top of shaft as shown on the Plans (i.e., the bottom of column at each Bent, and the bottom of
footing/pedestal at each Abutment). Where the shaft is extended below the design tip in accordance with Clarification 2.2, the added length shall be
paid at the Contract unit price per linear foot of Bid Item 421 up to a maximum added length of two (2) feet per shaft; added length in excess of two
(2) feet per shaft shall be compensated by Change Order pursuant to Contract §11 (Changes in the Work). Where the shaft is shortened above the
design tip in accordance with Clarification 2.2 (i.e., because rock was encountered higher than shown), the paid length shall be reduced by the actual
amount by which the shaft is shortened.
Clarification 2.4 — Temporary casing. Temporary casing to the top of rock, where the Contractor elects or is required to use casing for hole stability,
is considered subsidiary to Bid Item 421 and shall not be a separately paid item. Casing shall be advanced and removed in accordance with Sheet
B-17, Note 3, maintaining a minimum concrete head to prevent bond loss. Permanent casing in the rock socket is not required and shall not be
installed unless directed in writing by the Engineer.

PRE-BID MEETING MINUTES
1. ATTENDANCE
Owner — City of Milbrook
Engineer — Larkspur Civil Group, Inc.
Prospective Bidders
A sign-in sheet was circulated and is retained in the project bid file. Attendance at this pre-bid conference was non-mandatory; failure of a prospective bidder to attend does not disqualify a bid.
2. CALL TO ORDER
Marcus Okafor (Larkspur) opened the meeting at 10:00 a.m., introduced the project team, and stated the purpose of the conference: to walk prospective bidders through the scope, contract framework, and bidding schedule, and to receive written or verbal questions that will be addressed either in these minutes or by formal addendum. Mr. Okafor confirmed that the project was advertised on October 28, 2024, and that Bid Documents (Advertisement, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form, Contract, General & Special Conditions, Technical Specifications dated October 15, 2024, and the Plans dated for bidding) are available through the City's procurement portal.
Sam DeLuca (City Engineer) welcomed the bidders on behalf of the City of Milbrook and reiterated the City's commitment to a competitive, transparent bid process and to on-schedule delivery of the corridor improvement.
3. PROJECT OVERVIEW
Marcus Okafor presented the project scope, summarized as follows:
3.1 Corridor Widening.  Widening of Wren Parkway from an existing 2-lane rural section to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft shoulders and 6-ft sidewalks, extending 2.4 miles (approximately 12,600 linear feet) between the west limit at Old Millican Road (Sta. 100+00) and the east limit at McKinney Boulevard (Sta. 226+00).
3.2 Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement.  Complete removal of the existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge over Pecan Creek and construction of a new 285-ft three-span prestressed concrete girder bridge (spans of 90 ft — 105 ft — 90 ft), continuous for live load, founded on 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 8 ft into sound limestone at 40 ksf allowable end bearing. Abutment 1 (west) is at Sta. 167+00 and Abutment 2 (east) at Sta. 169+85; interior bents are at Sta. 167+90 (Bent 1) and Sta. 168+95 (Bent 2). Twelve drilled shafts total.
3.3 Ancillary Work.  Storm-drainage trunk system (12 runs) sized to a 25-year design storm using the Rational Method; MSE and reinforced-concrete retaining walls; pavement structure per the Typical Sections; signing, striping, and pavement markings; traffic-signal modification at the McKinney Boulevard intersection; illumination; MGS guardrail per Spec Section 606; and full erosion/sediment control under an approved SWPPP.
3.4 Scope Coordination Notes.
The corridor is under existing traffic; a Traffic Control Plan (TCP-01 through TCP-08) governs staged construction, temporary crossovers, and lane closures.
Utility relocations by others are shown on the Plans; contractor is responsible for coordination and daylighting per the Special Provisions.
The Pecan Creek 100-year peak flow governs demolition and construction sequencing at the bridge; the contractor is responsible for temporary works, dewatering, and coffer measures.
4. CONTRACT FRAMEWORK
Janet Kolb reviewed the contract framework:
Contract Type: Unit-price contract, 118 bid items on the Bid Form.
Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost Range: $23,000,000 to $26,000,000 (disclosed for planning use only; not a bid restriction).
Retainage: 5% held on earned value, released at Substantial Completion (per General Conditions §7.4).
Liquidated Damages: $2,400 per calendar day beyond the Contract Substantial Completion date (per Contract Article 4).
Prevailing Wages: Federal Wage Decision incorporated as Exhibit C; the City may withhold payment until wage underpayments are corrected and restitution paid (General Conditions §7.8).
Differing Site Conditions: Written notice under General Conditions §4.3 required; the condition must be materially different from those indicated in the Contract Documents.
Stored Materials: Bill of sale and off-site insurance required for payment on stored materials (General Conditions §5.6.2).
Bonds: Performance Bond and Payment Bond, each at 100% of the Contract Amount, issued by a surety acceptable to the City.
5. KEY DATES
The following schedule was reviewed:
Bids shall be submitted in duplicate hard copy in a sealed envelope marked with the Project Name, Project No. WP-2401, and the bidder's name, to the Office of the City Secretary, City of Milbrook, no later than 2:00 p.m. local time on November 12, 2024. Bids received after that time will not be accepted.
6. DBE PARTICIPATION GOAL
Sam DeLuca stated that this project is federally assisted under STP 2024(041) MK and is subject to the City's Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) Program. The contract-specific DBE participation goal is 8% of the total contract award value.
Each bidder shall submit, with its bid, the DBE Participation Schedule (Form DBE-1) identifying the DBE firms proposed for the work, the scope of work committed to each firm, and the dollar amount of participation. Alternatively, a bidder unable to meet the 8% goal shall submit a Good Faith Efforts documentation package (Form DBE-2) demonstrating adequate good-faith efforts prior to bid opening. Failure to submit either DBE-1 or DBE-2 by the bid deadline will render the bid non-responsive.
DBE directory lookups may be performed through the Texas Unified Certification Program (TUCP) database. Questions regarding DBE eligibility of specific firms shall be directed in writing to the City's DBE Liaison Officer prior to the bid opening.
7. QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
The following questions were received during the meeting. Where a question is addressed only in these minutes, this record is the sole documentation. Where a question requires a change to the Bid Documents, that change will be issued by formal addendum. Additional written questions will be accepted at jkolb@larkspurcivil.com until 3:00 p.m. on November 7, 2024.
Q-1 (Ironhorse — Petrov): Are the boring logs and geotechnical report by Redoak Geoscience LLC to be relied upon by bidders as the sole indication of subsurface conditions, particularly at Bent 2?
A-1 (Whitfield): The Geotechnical Data Report prepared and sealed by Lisa Fontaine, PE (Redoak Geoscience LLC), including the twelve boring logs B-1 through B-12, is included in the Contract Documents by reference and is available in the bid room and via the procurement portal. Bidders' attention is directed to Section 5.2 of that report, which specifically addresses the pinnacled character of the local limestone and notes that top-of-rock may fluctuate by approximately ±6 ft over lateral offsets on the order of thirty feet due to karst weathering. Boring B-7, located at Bent 2 (Sta. 168+95), records top of rock at elevation 512.3 (NAVD 88). Bidders are advised to review B-7 in conjunction with the §5.2 note in developing their means and methods and pricing for drilled-shaft production.
Q-2 (Vantera — Ballard): What datum controls elevations on the Plans, and how should the existing 1998 utility as-built information (referenced in the Utility Coordination Sheets) be reconciled with the current design?
A-2 (Okafor): All project elevations, structural and roadway, are referenced to NAVD 88. Horizontal control is NAD 83, Texas State Plane Central Zone, U.S. survey feet. The 1998 utility as-built information referenced in the coordination sheets was originally established on NGVD 29 and requires a datum conversion of +0.83 ft to be brought onto the project NAVD 88 basis. This is noted on the survey control memo included in the bid package. Bidders shall not rely on any as-built elevation without applying the noted conversion.
Q-3 (Bluebonnet — Alderman): Sheet C-12 shows storm drain Line B-2 as a 24-inch RCP. Given the tributary area, the bidder's independent capacity check indicates the run is marginal. Please confirm the intended pipe size.
A-3 (Okafor): The Engineer acknowledges the question and confirms that a review of the drainage calculations for Line B-2 is in progress. Addendum No. 1, anticipated for issue on or before November 8, 2024, will reissue Sheet C-12 as C-12R with Line B-2 upsized to 30-inch RCP. Bidders shall bid the addendum-revised size once Addendum No. 1 is issued; acknowledgment of Addendum No. 1 on the Bid Form is mandatory. The Storm-Drainage Design Report (Section 4) will be revised accordingly.
Q-4 (Concho — Escareño): Please confirm the design storm criteria for the storm-drain trunk and for the Pecan Creek crossing.
A-4 (Whitfield): The storm-drain trunk system is designed to a 25-year recurrence-interval design storm using the Rational Method (Q = C · i · A) with IDF data from the Milbrook Drainage Criteria Manual. The Pecan Creek waterway opening, scour analysis, and bridge low-chord clearance are governed by the 100-year recurrence-interval flood, with peak discharge of 4,120 cfs and a 100-year water-surface elevation of 522.4 ft (NAVD 88) at the bridge. The scour analysis follows FHWA HEC-18 / HEC-23.
Q-5 (Summit — Rowe): Please confirm the guardrail system and mounting height at the bridge approaches. Section 606 references a 31-inch MGS. Is the approach rail height governed by that specification, or by a different requirement?
A-5 (DeLuca): Bidders shall bid the guardrail system as shown on the Plans and specified in Technical Specification Section 606 as issued for bid. Any refinement to the approach-rail mounting height, if directed by the City after award to reflect the programmed 3-inch pavement overlay and preserve effective height above the crashworthy minimum, will be handled as a construction-phase directive under the Contract and will not be part of this bidding cycle. Bidders shall not price contingent alternates for guardrail height.
Q-6 (Vantera — Ballard): Please confirm the prevailing wage decision applicable to the project and the certified-payroll reporting cadence.
A-6 (Kolb): The applicable federal wage decision is attached to the Contract as Exhibit C — Federal Wage Decision and is incorporated by reference through General Conditions §7.8. Certified payrolls shall be submitted weekly on Form WH-347 (or equivalent), with signed Statement of Compliance, covering all workers of the Contractor and every subcontractor and lower-tier subcontractor performing work on the project site. Payrolls are due by close of business on the Wednesday following each pay-week ending. Failure to submit compliant certified payrolls, or the presence of uncorrected wage underpayments, may result in withholding of progress payments in accordance with §7.8 until corrections are made and restitution is paid.
Q-7 (Ironhorse — Hines): Are drilled-shaft integrity tests (CSL or thermal) required on the twelve bridge shafts, and if so, how is the testing paid?
A-7 (Whitfield): Cross-hole sonic logging (CSL) is required on every drilled shaft on the project (twelve shafts total). CSL access tubes shall be furnished and installed as specified in Section 416, and the testing is performed by the City's independent testing agency (Pinnacle Testing Services LLC). The installation of access tubes and the Contractor's coordination with the testing agency is subsidiary to the drilled-shaft unit price. Retesting, if triggered by an anomaly, is at the Contractor's expense per the Special Provisions.

GENERAL NOTES
1. This drawing depicts the sanitary sewer trunk main constructed under City of Milbrook Contract 97-U-11 during the period April 1998 through October
    1998. All information shown reflects field measurements taken by City forces during construction and post-construction survey verification completed
    October 27–29, 1998.
2. All elevations shown on plan and profile, in the manhole schedule, and in the invert-el          ble are referenced to NGVD 29 and were established from
    City of Milbrook Bench Mark BM-14 (brass disk in the concrete headwall at the Old Millican Road / Pecan Creek crossing, published elevation 528.62 ft
    NGVD 29).
3. Horizontal alignment is referenced to the Milbrook City Grid (1976), tied to City monuments MK-7 (Sta. 100+00) and MK-9 (Sta. 226+00).
4. The Pecan Creek Interceptor runs generally parallel to and north of Pecan Creek within a permanent utility easement of variable width (15 ft minimum)
    recorded at Hays County Volume 1198, Page 442.
5. Pipe material: 18-inch nominal diameter ductile iron sanitary sewer pipe, Class 52, push-on joint, with approved coal-tar epoxy interior lining, in accordance
    with City Standard Specification 02730 (1996 ed.).
6. Bedding: Type "B" per City Standard Detail SS-D-4, crushed limestone bedding 6 in below pipe and 12 in above pipe crown; native clay backfill above.
7. Manholes: 48-inch precast concrete manholes in accordance with City Standard Detail SS-D-9. All frames and covers are Neenah R-1642 or approved equal.
8. Depth of cover varies from 8.4 ft (MH-A-14) to 14.7 ft (MH-A-17). Line is entirely gravity flow at design slope of 0.0028 ft/ft between MH-A-15 and
    MH-A-17.
9. Utility crossings identified during construction are noted on the profile. Two crossings were made within the reach shown: an existing 12-inch water main at
    approximate Sta. 166+40 (crossed above the sewer, clearance 2.1 ft) and an existing 4-inch gas main at approximate Sta. 170+15 (crossed above the sewer,
    clearance 1.8 ft).
10. The 1962 timber-pile bridge carrying Wren Parkway over Pecan Creek crosses the interceptor alignment between Sta. 168+50 and Sta. 169+40.
    Construction of the interceptor within this reach was carried out by hand-excavation between existing timber pile bents to avoid contact with the bridge
    substructure. Field-measured clearance from top of pipe to underside of bridge Bent No. 2 pile cap was 3.6 ft at closest approach.
11. Rock was encountered in trench excavation between approximate Sta. 168+40 and Sta. 169+10, requiring pneumatic breaker and limited controlled blasting
    (single-hole detonators, 0.5 lb charges, per City-approved blasting plan dated 07/18/1998). See Field Note Book 98-6, pages 118–134, for detail.

Parkway bridge over Pecan Creek and associated roadway widening improvements in the City of Milbrook, Hays County,
Texas.

Nationwide Permit 14 (Linear Transportation Projects), as reissued in the Federal Register on January 13, 2021 (86 FR 2744),
with an effective date of March 15, 2021, and an expiration date of March 14, 2026. The nationwide permit, its general
conditions, the Texas Regional Conditions, and the TCEQ Section 401 Water Quality Certification conditions are incorporated
into this verification by reference, per the citations in the Referenced Materials list below.
1. PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The verified work consists of the replacement of an existing two-span steel-girder bridge (constructed in 1962) over Pecan Creek
with a new 285-foot, three-span (90 ft - 105 ft - 90 ft) prestressed concrete girder structure supported on 48-inch drilled shafts
founded in limestone, together with associated roadway widening of Wren Parkway from a two-lane rural section to a four-lane
divided urban section with 8-foot shoulders and 6-foot sidewalks, over a total length of approximately 2.4 miles between Old
Millican Road (west limit, Station 100+00) and McKinney Boulevard (east limit, Station 226+00). The new bridge will be
constructed on the existing alignment following demolition and removal of the existing structure.
Work within jurisdictional waters of the United States is limited to:
 a. Temporary placement of a rock-and-fabric work platform and cofferdam materials at proposed Bent 2 (Station 168+95),
     impacting approximately 0.03 acre (1,308 sf) of the ordinary high-water channel of Pecan Creek. All temporary fill will
     be removed and pre-project contours restored upon completion of substructure construction.
 b. Permanent placement of two drilled-shaft columns (48-inch diameter, two shafts per bent) at Bents 1 and 2, resulting in a
     permanent loss of approximately 0.008 acre (348 sf) of Waters of the United States below the ordinary high-water mark.
 c. Placement of scour-protection riprap around Abutments 1 and 2 and Bent 2, with a governing D50 of 18 inches keyed to
     and covered by native streambed material, resulting in a permanent conversion of approximately 0.09 acre (3,920 sf) of
     unvegetated channel bottom.
 d. Demolition of the existing 1962 bridge, including removal of two existing intermediate bent columns and abutment
     wingwalls within the channel, with a corresponding net gain of approximately 0.02 acre of open-water channel following
     removal.
Total permanent impact to Waters of the United States is approximately 0.098 acre, which is within the 0.5-acre threshold
established under NWP 14. No jurisdictional wetlands were delineated on-site by Redoak Geoscience LLC in the July 2, 2024,
aquatic-resources delineation report. No stream mitigation is required for the permanent impacts at this quantity; nevertheless,

 the impact minimization measures described in your PCN (turbidity curtains, timing restrictions, riprap key-in below
streambed grade, and full restoration of temporary work areas) shall be implemented as project conditions of this verification.
The 100-year discharge for Pecan Creek at the crossing is 4,120 cubic feet per second, with a design velocity at Bent 2 of 6.9
feet per second and a 100-year water-surface elevation of 522.4 feet (NAVD 88). Scour analysis performed under FHWA
